content:
We are excited to launch Lean Machine Learning, a project dedicated to formalizing machine learning theory in the Lean proof assistant.

The Lean Machine Learning library aims to provide carefully designed definitions and fundamental theorems spanning the major sub-areas of machine learning, together with extensive documentation and tutorials to make it accessible to the machine learning community. We also plan to develop tools that make it more convenient to write machine learning algorithms in Lean.

The project website is available at https://leanmachinelearning.org/, and the repository is available at https://github.com/leanmachinelearning/LML.

The project is still in its early stages, and we invite everyone interested to contribute. For this launch, we have formalized a sequential decision-making framework and used it to prove regret bounds for two well-known stochastic bandit algorithms: explore-then-commit (ETC) and upper confidence bounds (UCB). We are working on proving additional results within this framework, including a Bayesian regret bound for Thompson sampling, as well as error bounds for optimization algorithms. This is just the beginning.

While current LLMs can certainly speed up the formalization process, our focus on trustworthy, general and reusable definitions means that human-led design, development, and revision are a core priority. As a Mathlib maintainer, I consider giving back to Mathlib another core priority. We plan to follow Mathlib conventions as closely as possible while providing definitions at the right level of generality for machine learning research.

We will host a Zoom meeting on 2026-05-19T17:00:00+02:00 via this zoom link to discuss the project, including its initial directions and plans for the future, and answer any questions you might have. Please join us if you are interested in learning more.

Discussion about this project will happen on the #Lean Machine Learning channel of this Zulip. Please join us there to ask questions, share ideas, and coordinate contributions.

On behalf of the Lean Machine Learning maintainers,
Rémy Degenne
The LML launch meeting begins in 20 minutes.
